title: Clip across the lamp without starting a fire
story: A 6 V battery lights a 12 Ω lamp. A real battery has a little resistance inside it; here it is drawn as R_int = 0.5 Ω. Two test clips hang across the lamp's terminals, and you must clip one of three things between them: an open switch (just a gap), a closed switch (a plain wire) or a second 12 Ω lamp. Choose the one that leaves the lamp shining normally and keeps the battery from working too hard.

goals.label: the lamp still carries 0.4 to 0.55 A
the lamp still sees 5.5 to 6.5 V
the battery delivers less than 0.6 A

hints: An open switch is a gap: no current crosses it, so it changes nothing, and the full lamp voltage appears across it.
A closed switch is a wire. A wire across the lamp gives the current a path with almost no resistance. What does the lamp see then, and what does the battery have to push?
A second lamp in parallel keeps the first one lit, but the battery has to supply both.
